correctness.rationale: The Gaussian score MGF gives the first four posterior cumulants by differentiation. Pearson inequality is reproved as a nonnegative squared residual, giving its equality condition. Substitution yields the score-jet forms; positivity of Gaussian likelihood preserves support; exact two-point moments and Bayes odds give recovery. Finite verifier checks algebra but the theorem rests on the analytic proof.

originality.rationale: The 2026 source establishes the posterior MGF from the conditional score, older exponential-family work establishes broad posterior-cumulant identities, and Pearson inequality is classical. The accepted contribution is their sharp composition into a local Gaussian-convolution score-jet constraint together with the global two-point prior equality characterization and explicit one-jet recovery. Targeted literature and published-record searches did not locate that combined statement or a stronger statement implying it; access residuals are recorded.
residual_risks: Full text of arXiv:2609.11136v1 was not directly retrievable; a detailed public exposition supplied the exact MGF formula.
Full 1993 JASA article was inaccessible, so an older equivalent inequality under exponential-family terminology cannot be excluded completely.
The theorem is necessary locally, not a complete characterization of globally realizable Gaussian-convolution score functions.

value.rationale: The theorem gives a necessary consistency check for fitted conditional scores that is strictly stronger than nonnegative posterior variance. Its sharp boundary has structural value: one local equality identifies and reconstructs a globally two-point conditional prior. The explicit density proportional to \(\exp(-y^4/4)\) passes the variance test yet violates the new condition.
